title: A workspace. A few layers. Every file connected.
intro: Tandem is a self-hosted chat workspace. The browser and desktop share a React interface and a client replica; a Node server owns the workspace's SQLite database, media and ordered events. This atlas connects the files to that behavior, then explains what changed and the evidence behind it.

areas.title: Shared interface
areas.summary: React screens, conversation rows, dialogs, accessibility and device preferences. This layer translates user intent into client operations.

areas.title: Client state & recovery
areas.summary: HTTP, socket replication, drafts, a durable outbox, attachments and WebRTC. Keeps an account's local state coherent across disconnects.

areas.title: Shared contract
areas.summary: Entities, REST/socket events, permissions, search grammar and huddle types. Server and client agree on shapes and meaning here.

areas.title: Workspace authority
areas.summary: Validated requests, SQLite transactions, event publication, identity, integrations, files, retention and recovery.

areas.title: Desktop & local hosting
areas.summary: Electron owns native storage, IPC, the embedded host, backup workers, renderer recovery and close preparation.

areas.title: Browser entry
areas.summary: Vite assembles the shared interface for a browser. The server delivers cached compressed assets; device records stay in browser storage.

areas.title: Standalone host
areas.summary: A bundled Node entry can serve the same workspace without Electron. Docker packages this route for self-hosting.

areas.title: Build & verification
areas.summary: Build identity, archive and byte guards, test fixtures, CI, measurement probes and release gates connect shipped artifacts to their inputs.

areas.title: Research archive
areas.summary: Dated probes, reports and raw results preserve why a change was proposed. A successful diagnostic can establish a defect rather than repair it.

areas.title: Decisions & operations
areas.summary: Deployment instructions, implementation records, validation boundaries and future work. Plans are distinguished from implementation evidence.

areas.title: Workspace configuration
areas.summary: The package manager, dependency lock, shared compiler settings, contribution policy and repository-level commands.

areas.title: This atlas
areas.summary: Reviewed explanations and a deterministic generator turn repository files into this portable page. The generated page excludes itself from its own inventory.

principles.title: The server decides
principles.text: SQLite and authorized event publication define durable workspace truth. Optimistic client state still has to reconcile with the server's reply.

principles.title: Local work needs an owner
principles.text: A draft or queued send belongs to an account and conversation. Durable acknowledgements, revisions and tombstones prevent stale windows from silently losing or reviving work.

principles.title: A lifetime crosses awaits
principles.text: An async reply can arrive after a dialog, microphone intent or host changes. Generation checks, per-view state and retained resource ownership keep the result with the action that started it.

principles.title: Optimize against evidence
principles.text: Indexes, bounded work, stable references and import boundaries address specific costs. Read the fixture and limits before treating a historical benchmark as a general speed claim.

reading.title: Start with the map
reading.text: Click an architecture block to open its entry file. Follow the dependencies to see which layer performs each operation.

reading.title: Follow a real journey
reading.text: How it works explains an operation step by step, with the files responsible for each handoff.

reading.title: Inspect the implementation
reading.text: File explorer has reviewed runtime summaries, complete text source, declarations with line links, named tests, imports and reverse references. Press / to search file paths; enable source search to find code.

reading.title: Check a claim
reading.text: Improvements distinguishes implemented controls, historical measured changes and open follow-ups. Evidence links open the embedded original report or raw results.

limits: This is a source snapshot, not a live monitor. Its input digest identifies the embedded files; regenerate it after changes. The base commit identifies the checkout, not a claim that all local files were committed there.

Every tracked file is indexed except this generated HTML itself. Explicit atlas source files are added before their first commit. Ignored builds, node_modules, user data and unrelated untracked directories are not scanned.

All runtime source files in apps and packages have reviewed file explanations. Test, research, documentation, configuration and asset descriptions also use structural metadata. Generated symbol and import indexes do not infer every line's intent.

Imports are static source references, including literal dynamic imports and workspace package entries. They are not a runtime call graph; type-only imports, indirect exports and injected adapters can change how the code runs.

Text source is complete and paged for responsive reading. Binary assets show metadata. Symbol indexing covers named declarations, class methods and top-level values, not every anonymous closure or generated declaration.

Benchmarks belong to their recorded revision, hardware, sample count and fixture. A smaller archive does not establish faster startup. Bundle-entry limits do not measure the full import closure or decoded media memory.

N01–N12 are completed scoped repairs. Q01–Q13 are reproduced follow-up findings. A repaired storage backend does not automatically fix its callers' preference races; bounded controller cleanup does not establish every adapter owns a partially started server.

Recorded validation excludes genuine installed upgrade/uninstall, physical microphone unplug, power loss or OS logoff, and second-device/public routing. Active database cleanup does not erase old backups or freed disk bytes.

glossary.meaning: The client's account-specific copy of server state, updated through snapshots, HTTP replies and ordered socket events.
Durably queued sends. Revisions resolve newer edits; removal tombstones keep a stale window from restoring an already delivered or discarded send.
Making an already committed mutation visible to authorized socket clients and integrations. Its failure must not misreport a successful durable write.
A token that says which async attempt still owns a result. Equal values alone cannot distinguish an older request from a newer identical one.
Bounds on work accepted or queued, with recoverable refusal when capacity is unavailable.
SQLite full-text search. Query shape and measured index selectivity determine how it combines with channel, author, date and cursor constraints.
Policy-driven removal of old workspace content, including whole-thread cleanup and invalidating copies and attachment caches.
The narrow bridge from Electron's renderer to privileged native work in its main process; sensitive calls authenticate the sender.
Median and 95th-percentile latency for one declared sample set. They need workload, hardware, error and spread context.
Revision and input hashes embedded in an artifact so checks can reject stale, changed or mismatched builds.
